title: Fast-path decoder conductor: kernel-tuned prefill scheduling, attention-fuse hooks, and graceful downgrade
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Prototype and validate a 'fast-path' decoder conductor that orchestrates prefill and decode scheduling based on kernel fingerprints and attention-fuse capability, plus an acceptance-scoring layer that allows immediate short-path returns with a deterministic graceful downgrade to wider models or standard decode when confidence is low. Scope includes scheduler, lightweight acceptance scorer, kernel selection hooks, fallback orchestration, and telemetry. Out of scope: changes to model training, long-form decode optimizations for >1024 tokens.
acceptance_criteria: Latency: median decode tail latency for short prompts (<=64 tokens) reduced by >=20% on targeted models under normal load compared to baseline
Correctness: acceptance scorer false-accept rate <=2% for short-path outputs on held-out acceptance set
Fallback reliability: when acceptance scorer rejects, fallback decode produces output within 2x latency of baseline 95th percentile
Safety: no increase in safety-filtered responses during canary compared to baseline
Observability: end-to-end traces and cost-per-token telemetry are emitted for 100% of fast-path attempts
Tests: unit+integration+perf harnesses pass in CI and on canary fleet
rollout_plan: Prototype: implement conductor and scorer behind feature flag; run microbenchmarks in dev cluster
Lab perf: run controlled A/B perf runs against synthetic workloads covering short/long prompt mixes
Canary: enable on 1% of production traffic for dedicated internal customers with verbose logging
Expand: 10% -> 30% -> 100% with post-step validation gates and automatic rollback criteria
Post-mortem: collect metrics and a 2-week retrospective before GA
test_plan: Unit: scorer threshold logic, kernel fingerprint matcher, scheduler priority queue behavior
Integration: conductor + runtime endpoint with fake models to validate acceptance and fallback paths
Perf: run long lived throughput tests with synthetic concurrency spectrum and measure cost/latency
Safety: run acceptance set and existing safety filters on outputs from accepted fast-path samples
Chaos: simulate kernel failures and degraded GPU throughput to verify graceful downgrades
notes: Design tradeoffs: tight thresholds increase false-rejects (higher cost) while loose thresholds increase risk of degraded output quality. We'll bias conservative at canary and iterate.
Kernel heuristics: use lightweight fingerprint (opset + attention-pattern + dtype + seqlen bucketing) to pick low-latency kernel path where available.
Attention-fuse: enable fuse hook only for models with verified attention kernel; fallback path must be able to run unfused attention without deadlocks.
Prefill scheduling: prefer scheduling prefill on same host as decoder KV cache when kernel match probability > 0.8 to avoid KV transfer overheads.
Resource accounting: fast-path should emit a token-cost estimate pre- and post-accept for accurate billing comparisons.
Risk: regression in output quality for conservative quantized kernels; include regression alerting tied to prompt-set evals.
